classification.difficultyReason: Construct and compare compound-interest and simple-interest expressions, simplify to a quadratic, and select the positive interest rate.

content.prompt: An investor invests $\$10\,000$ at $x\%$ p.a. compound interest for 2 years. He finds that he receives $\$20$ more in interest than if he had invested it at a simple interest rate of $x\%$ p.a. Find $x$, correct to two decimal places.

answer.short: $x=2\sqrt5\approx4.47$, so the interest rate is $4.47\%$ p.a.
answer.worked:
With interest compounded annually, the compound interest and simple interest, in dollars, are
$$\begin{align*}I_C&=10\,000\left[\left(1+\frac{x}{100}\right)^2-1\right]\\I_C&=200x+x^2\\I_S&=10\,000\left(\frac{x}{100}\right)(2)\\I_S&=200x.\end{align*}$$
The compound interest exceeds the simple interest by $\$20$, so
$$\begin{align*}(200x+x^2)-200x&=20\\x^2&=20\\x&=\pm2\sqrt5.\end{align*}$$
The investment earns interest, so take the positive rate: $x=2\sqrt5\approx4.47$. Thus the rate is $4.47\%$ p.a., correct to two decimal places.

Check using the exact value: the extra interest is $(2\sqrt5)^2=20$ dollars.
